tasks.title: Instruct the post-task reviewer to actually verify
tasks.description:
Task #77 grants the post-task reviewer git-inspection subcommands and the reviewed task's own test commands. That grant is INERT on its own: the reviewer's prompt never tells it to run anything, so it will keep reviewing from the diff text alone.

Edit `agents/post-task-reviewer.md` (this is the source of truth; `cairn init` copies it into each project's `.claude/agents/`). Add instructions telling the reviewer to:

1. Run the task's declared test commands and report the actual result — pass/fail plus relevant output — as part of its findings.
2. Use git inspection to go beyond the supplied diff where it helps, e.g. `git show <sha>:<path>` to see a file's pre-change version, or `git log` for surrounding history.
3. State explicitly when it could NOT verify something, rather than silently reviewing from the diff alone.

PRESERVE unchanged: the existing `internal: true` frontmatter, the "You may only write to the review file whose path is given in your user prompt — never modify `.cairn/tasks.json`" instruction, the ASCII coverage-diagram format with its [DONE]/[PARTIAL]/[GAP] markers, and the existing output template.

Note on propagation: agent prompts are resolved by `buildAgentArgs` (src/agent-prompt.ts:9) from `<projectRoot>/.claude/agents/<name>.md` — the project's own COPY — with no fallback to this bundled source. Editing `agents/post-task-reviewer.md` is correct and sufficient for this task; the user re-runs `cairn init` after the round to propagate. Do NOT edit `.claude/agents/post-task-reviewer.md` directly.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.
tasks.notes:
# Task #78 — Instruct the post-task reviewer to actually verify

## What changed

**`agents/post-task-reviewer.md`** (the source of truth; `cairn init` copies this
into `<project>/.claude/agents/post-task-reviewer.md` — did NOT touch the copy).

Added a new `## Verification` section, placed right after the existing "You may
only write to the review file..." instruction and before `## Coverage Diagram`.
It tells the reviewer to:

1. Run the task's declared test commands (the "Expected Tests" section of its user
   prompt, built by `buildPostTaskReviewUserPrompt` in `src/post-task-reviewer.ts`)
   and report the real pass/fail result plus relevant output — not a result it
   didn't actually observe. Covers the tool grant added by Task #77
   (`buildTestCommandRules` → `Bash(<cmd>:*)` rules), which was otherwise inert.
2. Use git inspection beyond the supplied diff — explicit examples: `git show
   <sha>:<path>` for a file's pre-change version, `git log` for surrounding
   history. Matches the `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES` grant from Task #77 (`git diff`,
   `log`, `show`, `status`, `rev-parse`).
3. State explicitly when something could not be verified, rather than silently
   falling back to diff-only review.

Added one more paragraph tying this back to the (unchanged) output template: since
the task explicitly required preserving the existing output format verbatim, I
didn't add a new "Test Results" heading. Instead the instructions say verification
findings should be folded into the existing Coverage/Gaps/Regression Risks
sections — a [DONE] marker should mean "I confirmed it," and unverifiable items get
a note inline in Gaps or Regression Risks rather than a new section.

## Preserved unchanged (per task instructions)

- `internal: true` frontmatter (line 4).
- The "You may only write to the review file whose path is given in your user
  prompt — never modify `.cairn/tasks.json`" instruction — untouched, my new
  section was added right after it.
- The ASCII coverage-diagram format with [DONE]/[PARTIAL]/[GAP] markers.
- The `## Output Format` section and its exact template (Coverage / Files Changed /
  Gaps / Regression Risks / Verdict, CLEAN/HAS_GAPS/HAS_RISKS rules) — byte-for-byte
  unchanged.

## Not touched

- `.claude/agents/post-task-reviewer.md` (the per-project copy) — per the task's
  explicit note, this is regenerated by `cairn init`, which the user runs after the
  round.
- `cairn.json` — untouched, as instructed.
- `src/post-task-reviewer.ts` — no code changes needed; Task #77 already built the
  tool-grant plumbing (`GIT_INSPECTION_RULES`, `buildTestCommandRules`). This task
  was purely the prompt-text half that makes those grants actually get used.

## Verification

- `bun run test` → 827 pass, 0 fail across 29 files (ran after the edit).
- Confirmed no test asserts exact byte-for-byte content of
  `agents/post-task-reviewer.md` beyond frontmatter/structural checks (grepped
  `test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts`, `test/agent-prompt.test.ts`,
  `test/commands/init.test.ts`, `test/commands/plan.test.ts` for references) — all
  still pass with the new section present.
- Health check not re-run (no `src/` changes in this task; markdown-only edit).

## For the next agent

If a future task wants the reviewer's test-run output to have its own dedicated
heading in the output template, that's a template change and should be done as its
own task (this one deliberately did not touch the template, per explicit
instruction).

tasks.title: New src/claude-settings.ts — safe merge helper for .claude/settings.local.json
tasks.description:
Create a new module `src/claude-settings.ts` that merges Cairn's permission rules into a project's `.claude/settings.local.json`. A user may already have this file from plain `claude` usage, so merging must be strictly non-destructive.

Requirements:

1. Read and parse the existing file when present. On MALFORMED JSON, fail loudly (throw or return a clear error) and NEVER clobber the file. Losing a user's hand-built permission list is the worst possible outcome here.
2. Union `permissions.allow` and `permissions.deny` by value, with dedupe. Create the `permissions` object and either array only if missing.
3. PRESERVE every other key untouched — `hooks`, `env`, `model`, `statusLine`, and any key this code does not recognize must round-trip unchanged. Do not drop unknown keys.
4. Write atomically. Follow the temp-file-replace pattern already used by `writeTasksFile()` in `src/tasks-file.ts` (around line 175).
5. Be idempotent: a second run with the same rules adds nothing and reports nothing.
6. Return which rules were actually added, so callers can report them.

DEDUPE DETAIL: Claude Code treats `Bash(x:*)` as sugar for `Bash(x *)` — they are equivalent. Canonicalize that trailing suffix form FOR COMPARISON ONLY so a user who wrote the spaced form does not accumulate an equivalent duplicate. Never rewrite or reformat a user's existing entry. Rules that differ BEFORE the suffix must stay distinct: `Bash(git:*)` and `Bash(git diff:*)` are different rules and both must survive.

CRITICAL TEST ISOLATION: every test must operate in a temp directory. A test that points this code at the real project root would rewrite THIS repository's actual `.claude/settings.local.json`, which currently holds 18 hand-accumulated rules. Never use the real projectRoot in a test.

TDD: create test/claude-settings.test.ts, write failing tests first (fresh-file creation, merge into existing, unknown-key preservation, malformed-JSON refusal, idempotency, suffix-equivalent dedupe), then implement.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.

tasks.title: Wire the settings.local.json writer into cairn init
tasks.description:
Use the merge helper from `src/claude-settings.ts` (task #79) to seed a permission baseline during `cairn init`.

In `runInit` (src/commands/init.ts, around line 472), add a step alongside the existing `installNarrationHooks` and `createInstructionsFile` prompts. PROMPT the user before writing, DEFAULTING TO YES — use the existing `promptBoolean` helper. Writing permission rules affects every Claude session in that project, so it gets a visible confirmation.

Rule set to merge:

ALLOW:
- Git inspection subcommands: `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`, `Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(git rev-parse:*)`. Never a blanket `Bash(git:*)`.
- Rules derived from the project's `cairn.json` values for `healthCheck` and `defaultTestCommand` (available from the config object init already builds). Skip cleanly when a value is empty.

DENY — exactly these five, no more:
- `Bash(cairn task start:*)`
- `Bash(cairn task complete:*)`
- `Bash(cairn task set-status:*)`
- `Bash(cairn task add:*)`
- `Bash(cairn task note:*)`

NEVER emit a blanket `Bash(cairn task:*)` deny. `commands/generate-tasks.md:149` requires `cairn task next-id` for ID allocation, deny beats allow regardless of specificity, and there is no mechanism to carve an exception back out — a blanket deny would silently break task generation in every project. `next-id` and `show` must remain allowed.

These denies exist because the reviewer's inability to mutate `tasks.json` previously depended on it having no Bash at all; task #77 removes that implicit lock. Denies bind the reviewer and planner but are bypassed by `cairn run` execution agents (which use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`), which is exactly the intended scoping.

GITIGNORE: print a WARNING telling the user to gitignore `.claude/settings.local.json` themselves. Claude Code only auto-ignores that file when Claude Code itself writes it, and the entry goes to the user's GLOBAL git excludes, not the repo — so a file Cairn creates first gets no ignore entry. Do NOT edit any `.gitignore` and do NOT touch global git config.

Report written rules using the existing `InstallOptions` / `skipUnchanged` / `log` reporting style used by `writeNarrationHooks` and `installMdDir`.

CRITICAL TEST ISOLATION: tests must use a temp projectRoot. Never point init at the real repository root — this repo's `.claude/settings.local.json` has 18 accumulated rules.

TDD against test/commands/init.test.ts. DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.

tasks.title: Add cairn task next-id to the planner's allowedTools
tasks.description:
`src/commands/plan.ts` (around line 166) spawns the interactive planning session with:

    '--allowedTools', 'Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,Agent',

But `commands/generate-tasks.md:149` requires the planning session to run `cairn task next-id --count <n>` to allocate task IDs. Because that command is not pre-approved, it prompts the user mid-generation in every project — friction sitting directly on the critical path of the core workflow.

Add a rule pre-approving `cairn task next-id` (prefix form, e.g. `Bash(cairn task next-id:*)`).

SCOPE STRICTLY to `next-id`. Do not add other `cairn task` subcommands, do not add git rules, and do not otherwise widen the planner — interactive prompt fatigue in general is deliberately NOT this round's target. Note that task #80 adds deny rules for the five MUTATING `cairn task` subcommands; `next-id` is deliberately excluded from those denies, and deny would beat this allow if the two ever overlapped.

TDD against test/commands/plan.test.ts: assert the emitted allowedTools string, then implement.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.

tasks.title: Mark planner, audit-planner and summarizer as internal agents
tasks.description:
`buildSystemPrompt` (src/commands/run.ts, around lines 63-86) injects an assigned specialist agent's file body verbatim into the executor's system prompt under the heading "SPECIALIST INSTRUCTIONS: You have been assigned as a specialist agent for this task. Follow these instructions in addition to your standard workflow."

It already guards against misuse: at around line 68, if the agent is marked `internal: true` it warns and falls back to the generalist prompt. But ONLY `agents/post-task-reviewer.md` carries that flag. `agents/planner.md`, `agents/audit-planner.md`, and `agents/summarizer.md` have NO frontmatter at all, so the guard never fires for them.

This is not hypothetical. Tasks #70 and #71 in the previous round both ran with `agent: planner`. Injecting `planner.md`'s body into an executor tells it to "Have a conversation with the user about what they want to accomplish", to "Focus on understanding and planning, not implementation details", and — worst — "ONLY write to planning-notes.md — do NOT write tasks.json or modify any other files". None of that is appropriate for a headless `claude -p` implementation agent, and there is no user present to converse with.

Add YAML frontmatter with `name`, `description`, and `internal: true` to all three files, matching the format already used in `agents/post-task-reviewer.md`.

VERIFY TWO THINGS before finishing:
1. That agent discovery actually parses the flag into `AgentInfo.internal` (see `src/types.ts` and the discovery helper) so the run.ts guard fires. Add or extend a test covering it.
2. That adding frontmatter does not break `buildAgentArgs` (src/agent-prompt.ts), which reads the WHOLE file including frontmatter and passes it as the agent prompt for `cairn plan` and `cairn summarize`. `post-task-reviewer.md` already has frontmatter and works this way, so there is precedent — confirm, do not assume.

Also confirm these three still appear in the `cairn plan` preflight's specialist listing where appropriate — `buildDynamicContext` in src/commands/plan.ts filters on `!a.internal`, so this change WILL remove them from that list. That is correct and intended (they are not executor specialists), but note it in your task notes.

Propagation: these are the bundled source files; each project's `.claude/agents/` copies refresh when `cairn init` is re-run. Do not edit `.claude/agents/*.md` directly.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.

tasks.title: CLAUDE.md — truth-up the tasks.json enforcement story
tasks.description:
Two corrections to `CLAUDE.md`'s "Agent workflow" section.

1. THE ENFORCEMENT SET IS NOW WRONG. CLAUDE.md says direct `Edit`/`Write` on `tasks.json` is "enforced two ways: the per-agent system prompt explicitly bans it, and the post-task reviewer runs with a directory-scoped allowlist covering only `<dataDir>/reviews/**`". There was an unstated THIRD lock: the reviewer had no Bash at all, so it could not run `cairn task set-status` either. Task #77 removes that lock by granting the reviewer git-inspection subcommands and the reviewed task's test commands.

   Document the actual enforcement set as it now stands: the prompt ban, the directory-scoped write allowlist, and the explicit `permissions.deny` rules on the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands that `cairn init` writes (task #80). Record two facts that are easy to get wrong:
   - Deny rules are NOT enforced under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so they do not bind `cairn run` execution agents. They bind the reviewer and planner, which run in normal permission mode. This asymmetry is intended.
   - The deny covers mutating subcommands ONLY. A blanket `Bash(cairn task:*)` would break `cairn task next-id`, which task generation requires; deny beats allow with no exception mechanism.

2. SCOPE THE BAN ITSELF. "Direct `Edit` or `Write` on `tasks.json` is forbidden" currently contradicts `commands/generate-tasks.md:159`, which explicitly instructs the planning session to write `.cairn/tasks.json` using the Write tool. Both are right in intent — the ban targets EXECUTION AGENTS mutating a live task list mid-round, whereas task generation authors the file wholesale between rounds. Add a clause saying so, so the two documents stop contradicting each other.

CRITICAL GUARD — DO NOT MODIFY `cairn.json`. Its `healthCheck` is currently pinned to a throwaway outfile (`bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`) and is USER-MANAGED for this round. CLAUDE.md documents the REAL value (`bun run build` / `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile dist/cairn`) and must continue to. While the round runs, CLAUDE.md and `cairn.json` will legitimately disagree about the health check. That disagreement is EXPECTED and must NOT be "fixed" in either direction. In a previous round exactly this trap caused the pinned value to be committed permanently.

tasks.title: README.md — document the permission rules init now writes
tasks.description:
Document the new `cairn init` behavior added in task #80.

Add to `README.md` — the Workflow > Initialize section is the natural home, with a cross-reference from Configuration if useful:

1. That `cairn init` offers to write permission rules to `.claude/settings.local.json`, and that the prompt defaults to yes but is skippable.
2. WHAT gets written: read-only git inspection subcommands, allow rules derived from the project's `healthCheck` and `defaultTestCommand`, and deny rules on the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands.
3. WHY: agents that verify a task actually landed — chiefly the post-task reviewer — need to run tests and inspect history. Without these rules a fresh project denies them outright in headless mode.
4. That EXISTING settings are MERGED, not replaced: `permissions.allow` and `permissions.deny` are unioned and every other key is preserved untouched. A user who already has settings from plain `claude` usage will not lose them.
5. That the user should add `.claude/settings.local.json` to their own gitignore — Cairn deliberately does not edit `.gitignore` or global git config, and Claude Code only auto-ignores that file when it writes the file itself.

Keep the existing README structure and table formatting conventions.

CRITICAL GUARD — DO NOT MODIFY `cairn.json`. Its `healthCheck` is pinned to a throwaway outfile and is user-managed for this round. Any disagreement between documentation and `cairn.json`'s current value is EXPECTED — do not reconcile it.
